concept.name: Pre-market session
concept.definition: Extended-hours trading that occurs before the regular session opens; in U.S. equities, pre-market trading typically begins as early as 4:00 a.m. ET and runs until the 9:30 a.m. open. It is part of what regulators call extended-hours or after-hours trading — trading outside regular trading hours.
concept.intuition: The warm-up window: overnight news gets traded before the official open, but with fewer participants and wider spreads.
concept.mechanics: Trades execute on ECNs and exchanges' extended sessions (Nasdaq accepts extended-hours orders from 4:00 a.m. ET); many order types are unavailable, LULD bands do not apply in the same way, and the pre-market flow feeds into the opening auction's indicative prices.
concept.failure_modes: Thin liquidity exaggerates moves: pre-market prices can gap and reverse violently at the open, and executions resting on stale overnight references can be far from where the stock will actually open.
concept.misconceptions: The pre-market 'price' is not the opening price — the official open is set by the opening auction, and heavy pre-market moves routinely fade once full liquidity arrives.
concept.example: A company reports earnings at 7:00 a.m. ET; its shares trade up 8% in the pre-market session before the 9:30 a.m. Opening Cross sets the official opening price.
